description: The GALAXY 399 focuses on developing innovative solutions in smart agriculture and geospatial data analysis. By satellite data, and environmental analysis tools, we provide farmers with the information and insights they need based on their specific requirements. Our goal is to make this information simple, accessible, and easy to understand, helping farmers make better-informed decisions. Our team is committed to innovation, building sustainable technologies for a better future in agriculture.
summary:
GALAXY 399 is a free, bilingual (English and Persian) web platform that turns NASA and space-agency open data into clear, field-level information for farmers. A farmer finds the farm on a satellite map and draws its boundary; GALAXY 399 then automatically gathers 20 years of NASA POWER climate data, recent NASA POWER soil wetness, global soil maps and 30 m Copernicus elevation data for that exact field. It shows the slope, runoff and erosion risk of the land, compares the farmer's harvest with the attainable yield from FAO GAEZ v5, suggests crop-rotation strategies that save water and protect the soil, and produces an integrated farm report. Every number is shown with its source, and missing data are shown as missing — never invented.
It matters because small farmers rarely receive information about their own field in a form they can understand and act on. GALAXY 399 helps them use water and soil more wisely and make better-informed decisions in a changing climate.
details:
Locate the farm. Interactive farm map: search for any place in the world, draw the field boundary on satellite imagery; map labels are in English.

Automatic farm scan. Place name, elevation, soil (ISRIC SoilGrids, FAO HWSD), 20 years of NASA POWER daily climate, the last 120 days of NASA POWER soil wetness and FAO GAEZ crop suitability are collected for the field.

Terrain and land health. From a 30 m Copernicus digital elevation model: elevation, slope in FAO classes, slope aspect versus field orientation, modelled runoff paths, ponding-prone spots, topographic wetness and erosion susceptibility (LS factor, optional RUSLE), with a 3D view and elevation profiles.

Crop yield gap. The farmer's own yield is compared with the attainable yield and the regional average yield from FAO GAEZ v5, with a simple verdict and practical tips.

Crop rotation planning. Rotation strategies (current practice, water saving, soil health, balanced) are built and scored with transparent agronomic rules and FAO-56 water balance, and compared side by side.

Integrated report. A 16-section farm report with the source and date of every value, exportable as PDF, JSON, CSV and GeoJSON.

Save, load and two languages. Work can be saved and loaded; the whole interface works in English and Persian.

GALAXY 399 is a browser application (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) with a small Python server that uses only the standard library. The server reads cloud-optimised GeoTIFF files (Copernicus DEM tiles, FAO GAEZ v5 rasters) with HTTP range requests, so only the pixels around the farm are downloaded; it also delivers ISRIC SoilGrids values reliably (retries and a 90-day cache) and stores saved work. Terrain analysis uses established methods: Horn (1981) slope and aspect, Priority-Flood depression filling, D8 flow routing, the Moore & Burch LS factor and the Williams (EPIC) soil erodibility factor. Crop water needs follow FAO-56.

·       Information about the farmer’s own field, not a regional average, in plain language and in two languages.

·       Free and open: no accounts, no API keys, public data only; every number shows where it comes from.

·       Honest about uncertainty: model limits are explained and missing data are never filled with invented values.

We want farmers to use water and soil more efficiently, choose crops and rotations that fit their land and climate, and protect their soil from erosion — and we want to make NASA Earth-observation data useful at the scale of a single field.

JavaScript, HTML and CSS; Python 3 (standard library); Leaflet, Leaflet-Geoman, Turf.js, Chart.js, geotiff.js and MapLibre GL JS; Microsoft Edge for testing.
